subject.title: feat(ui): complete Control UI MCP App bridge

question: Should MCP App `ui/message` remain strictly conversational, rejecting every host command prefix before consent, or may exact-text consent authorize host command execution?
rationale: The PR creates a sandbox-to-host capability boundary, and source inspection shows that the current implementation enforces only part of the stated plain-text policy; the permanent authority boundary needs explicit owner intent.

options.title: Keep messages conversational-only
options.body: Reject slash and bang command syntax centrally so sandboxed apps can request visible chat text but cannot invoke host command paths.

options.title: Permit commands with stronger consent
options.body: Explicitly define command-capable MCP Apps as product policy and add command-specific warnings, permission checks, documentation, and live security proof.

recommendation.title: Keep messages conversational-only
recommendation.body: Reject slash and bang command syntax centrally so sandboxed apps can request visible chat text but cannot invoke host command paths.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the self-assigned repository member driving the MCP App bridge and its security revisions, though an independent security or chat-command owner should review the final boundary.
